doc.title: Fred Wesley interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 21, 2024

title: Gold record and moving to Montgomery
summary: The gold record from the S.O.S. band; after his wife died he moved from South Carolina to Montgomery.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: Thank you for sharing that. That was actually the second last question. I wonder if you can tell me about that what looks like a gold record behind you.

Oh that’s just one of them. The rest — see I’m in Montgomery, Alabama. When my wife died in South Carolina, I lived in South Carolina for thirty years and my wife died and I came to Montgomery to visit my sister, who lives here in Montgomery. And I ran into my first girlfriend who lives here and she invited me to live with her. So reluctantly I moved little stuff, little stuff, little stuff out, and now everything I own is in this place. So that’s just one gold record. That was from the S.O.S. band that I did arranging for. Yeah. “Take Your Time, Do It Right” that was the name of the tune.
All right. Well this has been a fascinating chat and I really appreciate the time and the — your memories.
